error_direction_rationale: The kernel's outputs are set membership and string comparisons (name intersection, date ordering, label-aligned prefixes, inclusive bounds). No threshold or rounding approximation exists in any branch, so there is no direction in which errors could accumulate toward a finding or toward no-finding.

derived_from.clause_path: Overview / Capability Versioning / Intersection Algorithm / Extension Dependencies / Profile Resolution Flow
Overview / Profile Structure / Keys / Namespace Authority Binding / Namespace Governance / Version Format / Supported Versions / Component Versioning

branches.clause: Intersection Algorithm step 1: for each business capability, include it if a platform capability with the same name exists
Intersection Algorithm step 2 + Capability Versioning: exact version equality between profiles; highest shared version selected
Intersection Algorithm step 2: if the mutual version set is empty, exclude the capability from the intersection
Intersection Algorithm step 3: remove any capability where extends is set but none of its parents are in the intersection
Intersection Algorithm step 4: pruning is iterative; repeat until no more capabilities are removed
Extension Dependencies: requires.protocol min/max are inclusive bounds on the selected protocol version; violating extensions are excluded
Extension Dependencies: requires.capabilities maps names to inclusive min/max bounds on the selected versions of the named capabilities
Extension Dependencies: if requires is absent, the extension is assumed compatible with the profile's declared versions
Extension Dependencies / Profile Resolution Flow step 4: excluding an incompatible extension may orphan extensions that extend it, so orphan pruning repeats until the active set is stable
Profile Resolution Flow step 2: a platform that cannot support the requested protocol version fails the negotiation; supported_versions allows selecting a mutually supported older release
Profile Resolution Flow: negotiation failure (empty capability intersection) is a definite outcome
Namespace Authority Binding steps 1-6: reversed https schema host must equal the entity name or be a label-aligned prefix; on failure the entity is treated as not present and never activated
Component Versioning: a dev.ucp.* entry whose version differs from the profile's ucp.version MUST be rejected, treated as not present
Keys: the top-level keys[] member of a Profile is the canonical JWK Set key field
Supported Versions and Leaf Profiles: a party selecting an older version negotiates against the leaf profile for that version

assumption_of_use.value: the leaf profile document for the selected older protocol version
assumption_of_use.source: the supported_versions map in the pasted profile (location member per key)
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller — a verify-only node never fetches; it negotiates over the two pasted profile objects and reports the selected protocol version

branches.clause: Profile Resolution Flow step 3: for each intersected capability the platform fetches the schema document and validates the entity against it

assumption_of_use.value: the extension/capability schema documents named by entry schema members
assumption_of_use.source: the schema member of the pasted capability entries (namespace binding is checked; the document itself is not fetched)
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller — schema fetch and validation against the fetched document happen outside this kernel

branches.clause: Profile Resolution Flow steps 1-2: discovery failure and unsupported-protocol-version failure terminate negotiation at the transport layer

assumption_of_use.value: HTTP transport semantics (discovery status, error response bodies, continue_url flows)
assumption_of_use.source: the protocol transport binding, not the pasted profile objects
assumption_of_use.owner: the MCP worker transport layer — this kernel receives already-pasted profiles and raises no transport errors

branches.clause: Profile Structure: ucp.version, ucp.services, and ucp.payment_handlers MUST be present even when empty
Version Format: the protocol version MUST be a dated release in YYYY-MM-DD format; businesses MUST NOT advertise a non-date version string
Profile Structure: a Profile is a JSON object with a required ucp member
